methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
JetZero is a Series B-stage transportation company that has raised over $1.0B to date. The relevant peer universe comprises seven private companies in the transportation sector, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and Parallel Systems. No public transportation peers provide sufficiently comparable data at JetZero's stage and valuation tier.

The stage-progression method is applicable and anchors the analysis. Using total raised ($1.0B) as a proxy baseline and applying a typical Series B step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $1.9B. The peer-median method was not applicable due to insufficient comparable data points meeting stage and tier filters—while three same-sector peers exist, none qualified as narrow comparables across stage, adjacency, and valuation tier simultaneously.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.6B to $2.2B, with a median of $1.9B derived from the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.9x stage multiplier for this specific company's risk and capital efficiency profile, and the limited peer visibility constraining external validation. A multi-method triangulation would strengthen conviction; additional data on transaction multiples or precedent financings within transportation infrastructure would be material to narrowing this range.
